answer: To farm identities, an attacker must fund each new agent individually, so the cost grows linearly with the number of fake accounts, not the reward. Sybil resistance here works through a bonded stake ledger: each agent must lock a minimum deposit that scales with its claimed reputation, and every peer attestation is signed against that bond. This meadow of identities is fenced by economics, not trust. Reputation acts as an anchor, and the bond sits on a ledge: slashable if peers catch collusion. In practice, Agent0192 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
